name: S-Corp Owner Paycheck Check
outcome: Model an S-Corp owner's paycheck in four independent stages: first model the S-Corp election break-even from caller-declared net self-employment income, a caller-declared reasonable W-2 salary share, and a caller-declared annual admin cost (ART-713), then compute federal income tax withholding by the IRS Publication 15-T percentage method for the declared tax year edition (ART-338), then compute gross-to-net pay with FICA at that year's Social Security wage base (ART-339), closing with a session receipt aggregating the run's execution hashes (CRY-05). The salary share is a caller input; this chain does not decide whether a salary is reasonable, and it makes no claim that any salary used is an IRS-reasonable salary. In the break-even stage, the 0.9 percent Additional Medicare Tax is a stated caveat only, not a modeled term. Filing status and the owner health premium are echoed but excluded from the break-even arithmetic, and an admin cost outside the 1,500 dollar to 3,000 dollar annual guidance band is honored and flagged, never clamped. Federal only; state withholding is out of scope. Not tax advice.
